## BL-214 — Drill-through: one progressive-disclosure idiom

**Status: settled 2026-07-30.** Authority for the concept is `docs/ui/LAYOUT.md` § Drill-through
(new section, sibling to § Container vocabulary). This item lands the vocabulary, the shared
control, and the wiring of the six surfaces named below.

### The reframe: three axes, not four idioms

The four idioms were never four answers to one question. They were **three different questions**
wearing one costume. Naming the three is most of the fix:

| Axis | Question | Gesture | Control | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Depth** (this item) | *How much of this subject do I want?* | Expand **in place** | `ui::detail_stepper` — three-segment stepper | `ui_state::detail[]` |
| **Subject** (BL-196, built) | *What am I looking at?* | Click the element | Breadcrumb + `<` back | `ui_state::card_stack` |
| **Host** (SELECTION.md, built) | *Where does this properly live?* | `[>]` go-to | `ui::focus_on_entity` | `active_body` / `show_*` |

BL-196 is therefore **not folded in and not a competitor** — it is the sibling axis, and its
`card_stack`, breadcrumb and acyclicity rules are untouched. The Corporation dashboard's roll-ups
"clicking through into the relevant per-system ledger" are a **host** change, not depth, and are
correct as designed. Only the History explainer, the tile accordion's withheld derivation, and the
wizard's prose are depth.

### The closed set

```
GLANCE  — a figure and its direction. Labels, numbers, verdict words, glyphs. No sentences.
READ    — the compact composed view. + charts (with full legends: swatch · label · value)
          and interactive sub-controls (pagers, scrubbers, action grids).
STUDY   — the full derivation. + wrapped prose, threshold captions, annotated axes,
          derivation breadcrumbs, secondary/wide table columns.
```

**Content class table** — the only thing an implementer needs to decide where a widget belongs:

| Content class | Glance | Read | Study |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| Load-bearing figures, labels, verdict words, glyphs | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| Charts and their legends (swatch · label · **value**) | — | ✓ | ✓ |
| Interactive sub-controls (pagers, scrubbers, action grids) | — | ✓ | ✓ |
| Wrapped prose (explainers, consequences, why-lines) | — | — | ✓ |
| Threshold **captions**, annotated axes, derivation breadcrumbs | — | — | ✓ |
| Secondary / wide table columns beyond identity + key numerics | — | — | ✓ |

Note the threshold **line** is a chart element (Read); only its **caption** is Study. Legend
**values** stay at Read: a legend value is a load-bearing figure and demoting it would be
truncation by another name.

### Two invariants

1. **Levels are strictly additive.** A higher level never removes a load-bearing figure a lower
   level showed. The whole model is one monotone predicate —
   `shows(s, ui, want) == (detail_level_of(s, ui) >= want)` — and every content site is a single
   `if (shows(...))` with **no `else`**, no per-level layout variant, and no re-layout on change.
   This is what makes "expand, don't replace" fall out of the implementation instead of out of
   discipline.
2. **Every guaranteed-fit container is Glance-only.** LAYOUT.md containers **2** (on-canvas lens
   legend), **4** (header/balance strip), **5** (time panel), **7** (minimap lens bar) and
   **9-numeric** (table cells) offer no depth control at all. Levels only ever grow inside a
   **wrap** container (1, 3, 6, 9-description). Consequence: **drill-through adds no tenth
   container.** The nine say *how text fits*; the three say *how much text there is*. No level
   change can create a new overflow site.

### The authored policy table

`def` is **authored, never computed** — a default derived from the live region would twitch on
resize. The authoring criterion is: *the level at which the surface answers its own question in
one screenful at **1280×720***. `lo` follows a derived rule: a **fixed-rect** container's `lo` is
the level its rect was authored for; a **stretch/scroll** container's `lo` may be `glance`.

| `detail_surface` | lo | hi | **def** | What each level is, here |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `selection_band` | read | study | **read** | Fixed 340 px rect (`selection_band_height`) authored for Read — Glance would leave it half-empty. Read = today's content (hex neighbourhood + accordion + action grid, or the action\|facts split). Study adds the accordion's threshold captions and the tile derivation breadcrumb. |
| `selection_drill` | read | study | **read** | Same fixed rect. Read = the BL-196 time series + scrubber. Study adds the annotated axis and the "Recording began here…" provenance line. |
| `history_story` | glance | study | **read** | Glance = the archetype + span line only. Read = the dated `ev.event` lines. Study = + each line's indented `ev.consequence` paragraph. Read is the view's question, so Read is the default. |
| `history_chain` | glance | study | **glance** | Glance = one verdict line per stage in the round (`Lost here: Cinder` / `all passed`), which fits the 324 px column in one screenful. Read = + each stage's charts. Study = + `stage_explainer()` prose and threshold captions. Four stages of charts do **not** fit one screenful — this is the rule producing the answer, not an assertion. |
| `history_tiles` | read | study | **read** | Read = X / Y / composition / landform / hazard / habitability. Study = + the 23 per-resource columns (today's horizontal-scroll offender). |
| `generation_wizard` | read | study | **study** | **The one named exception** to the default criterion (see below). Read strips the explainers for a replaying player. |

**The wizard exception, stated explicitly rather than by omission.** `generation_wizard` does not
fit Study in one screenful and gets Study anyway, because for this surface the depth *is* the
feature (BL-167: "the first thing a player sees"). It participates rather than being exempt for
three reasons: it becomes the **teacher** of the idiom (the gesture is learned before the first
ledger opens); a Read rung is a real want an exemption would have destroyed (a replaying player
wants the charts without the chemistry); and "first contact" is an argument about first contact,
which the **reset-to-Study-on-entry** rule honours exactly.

### Memory

The chosen level is **remembered per surface, for the session** (`ui_state::detail`), and is
**not serialised** — the same policy as `economy_view` / `history_view`. A **subject** change
(selecting a different tile, switching the History body combo) does **not** reset it; that is the
point of remembering. A **new campaign** resets it via `ui::reset_detail_levels(ui_state&)`, which
also runs on entering the generation screen from the main menu so the wizard always opens at Study.
A BL-196 drilled frame opens at its parent's level, **clamped** to `selection_drill`'s own range.

### The control

`ui::detail_stepper(detail_surface, ui_state&)` — a composite control, **not** a `ui::icons` glyph
(the icons contract is `(dl, centre, r, colour)`; a lit-segment count does not fit it, and no
ICONS.md entry is owed).

- **Placement, identical on every surface:** the surface's title row, right-aligned, immediately
  **left** of the `[>]` go-to / `[x]` close cluster.
- **Shape:** one `ImGui::InvisibleButton("##depth", {h * 2.2f, h})` with `h = GetFrameHeight()`,
  hit-split into three equal columns. Draws three baseline-aligned rounded bars of ascending
  height (`0.35h / 0.60h / 0.85h`) — the shape says *amount*. Segments at index ≤ current lit with
  `palette::selection`; higher segments at ~35 % alpha; segments outside `[lo, hi]` at ~15 % alpha
  and not clickable.
- **Draws nothing at all** when `lo == hi` (a single-level surface has no control).
- Hover tooltip: `Detail: Read  (Glance / Read / Study)`.
- **Not a toggle.** Exempt as a cross-cutting selector — the level set has **no null member**, so
  there is nothing to undo *to*, exactly as re-picking a resource in a lens combo is a no-op. This
  is recorded in LAYOUT.md citing the standing rule's existing exemption clause;
  `.claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md` is **not** edited. Re-clicking the active segment is a no-op
  — deliberately **not** "revert to default", which would be the locally-clever/opaque option and
  would make this the one control in the app whose re-click means *revert* while adjacent
  `nav_button` strips' re-click means *close*.
- **No keyboard binding, and it does not join the Esc ladder** (`app.cpp`, order today:
  `confirm_exit_pending` → `show_system_menu` → pop `card_stack` → hide selection → open system
  menu). Depth is not a dismissal; `card_stack` (subject) already owns that unwind, and a second
  one would re-merge the axes at the keyboard.

### Code shape

**New pair `src/ui/detail_level.{hpp,cpp}`.** No `CMakeLists.txt` edit is needed —
`file(GLOB_RECURSE GAME_SOURCES CONFIGURE_DEPENDS "src/*.cpp")` (CMakeLists.txt:89) picks it up.
Enums sit at **global** scope alongside `canvas_level` / `overlay_mode` (the file's existing
convention); functions sit in `namespace ui`. `struct ui_state;` is forward-declared so
`ui_state.hpp` may include this header without a cycle.

```cpp
// src/ui/detail_level.hpp
#pragma once
#include <cstdint>

struct ui_state; // fwd — the widget takes it by reference only

/// The closed set of disclosure levels (BL-214). Ordered: higher = strictly more
/// content. Levels are ADDITIVE — a higher level never removes a load-bearing
/// figure a lower one showed. See docs/ui/LAYOUT.md § Drill-through.
enum class detail_level : std::uint8_t
{
    glance = 0, ///< Figures, labels, verdict words, glyphs. No sentences.
    read   = 1, ///< + charts (with full legends) and interactive sub-controls.
    study  = 2, ///< + wrapped prose, threshold captions, annotated axes, wide columns.
};

/// Every site that owns a depth control. Indexes ui_state::detail.
/// Adding a surface = an enumerator here, a row in detail_policy_of, and one
/// `shows()` branch per gated content class. Nothing else.
enum class detail_surface : std::uint8_t
{
    selection_band = 0, ///< Selection band root content (selection_panel.cpp).
    selection_drill,    ///< A BL-196 drilled frame in the band (selection_card.cpp).
    history_story,      ///< History ledger, Story view (tile_inspector.cpp).
    history_chain,      ///< History ledger, Chain view.
    history_tiles,      ///< History ledger, Tiles view.
    generation_wizard,  ///< The New World wizard (app.cpp draw_generation_screen).
    count
};
inline constexpr std::size_t detail_surface_count =
    static_cast<std::size_t>(detail_surface::count);

/// What one surface declares: the inclusive level range it can render, and where
/// it opens. Authored, never computed at runtime — a default derived from the live
/// region would twitch on resize. lo <= def <= hi always.
struct detail_policy { detail_level lo, hi, def; };

namespace ui {
const detail_policy& detail_policy_of(detail_surface s);
void         reset_detail_levels(ui_state& ui);                       ///< All surfaces -> their def.
detail_level detail_level_of(detail_surface s, const ui_state& ui);   ///< Clamped to the policy.
bool         shows(detail_surface s, const ui_state& ui, detail_level want); ///< THE predicate.
bool         detail_stepper(detail_surface s, ui_state& ui);          ///< true on frames the level changed.
} // namespace ui
```

**State** — one line in `ui_state` (`src/ui/ui_state.hpp`), beside the `economy_view` /
`history_view` block it shares a policy with:

```cpp
    /// Per-surface disclosure level (BL-214), one entry per detail_surface, values
    /// are detail_level. VIEW state: remembered for the session so a player who asks
    /// for depth keeps it across reopens and across subject changes; NOT serialised
    /// (same policy as economy_view / history_view). Seeded by ui::reset_detail_levels.
    std::array<std::uint8_t, detail_surface_count> detail{};
```

**The wiring is uniformly one branch per site.** Worked example, `generation_charts.cpp`:

```cpp
    const bool study = (lvl >= detail_level::study);
    if (study) dim_para(stage_explainer(s));
    // `Lost here: Cinder` is a label + list — a GLANCE-class verdict, always drawn.
    if (lvl >= detail_level::read) { /* the chart_row() calls */ }
    // Caption gated, LINE not: auto cap = [&](const char* c){ return study ? c : nullptr; };
    charts::threshold_line(dl, mn, mx, 1.0512f, c, col_gate, cap("runaway greenhouse"));
```

`charts::threshold_line` gains a two-line guard: a null/empty `caption` draws the line and skips
the caption. That single change removes, at the default level, the `"ay greenhouse"` clip
committed in `scripts/verify/golden/history_chain_round0.png` today.

**Header factoring (foundation).** The three structurally-identical Selection headers —
generic (`selection_panel.cpp` ~:1186-1219), tile (~:590-604), drill (`selection_card.cpp` :36-62)
— become one `ui::draw_selection_header(...)`, so the stepper is added once rather than in three
places kept in sync. This is the recon's own recommendation and is a prerequisite, not a
nice-to-have: adding the stepper to three copies is how the fourth idiom gets born.

### Relationship to BL-215 (shared file scope — plan the collision)

The seam, stated flatly so neither item does the other's work:

> **BL-214 decides WHETHER a string is drawn. BL-215 decides HOW a string that is drawn fits its
> container.** A withheld paragraph is not a BL-215 fix; a clipped chart title is not a BL-214 fix.

**BL-214 lands first**, so BL-215's render-precision audit measures the reduced set. The two share
`docs/ui/LAYOUT.md`, `src/ui/charts.cpp`, `src/ui/generation_charts.cpp`,
`src/ui/selection_panel.cpp` and `src/ui/tile_inspector.cpp` — run them sequentially in one batch,
not as concurrent worktree agents.

### Extension recipe (so surface #7 does not invent idiom #5)

Adding a surface to the ladder is exactly three edits: an enumerator in `detail_surface`; a row in
`detail_policy_of` (with `lo` from the fixed-rect/stretch rule and `def` from the one-screenful-at-
1280×720 criterion); and one `if (shows(...))` per gated content class. `ui::detail_stepper` is
called once on the surface's title row. Nothing else — no new control, no new state, no new doc
section. The Corporation dashboard's four roll-ups (MENU.md slot 1, not yet built) are the first
expected caller; the enumerator is deliberately **not** added ahead of the wiring.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben was unavailable; these are authoritative and auditable.

1. **Three levels — Glance / Read / Study — as a closed set**, declared per surface as an inclusive
   range `[lo, hi]` plus a `def`, not as three mandatory rungs. Two rungs is the collapse that
   produced the problem; four-plus is a spectrum, not a vocabulary.
2. **The uniform gesture is one shared stepper with expand-in-place as the only response** — and
   the answer *names the other two gestures* (subject / host) so they stop competing. BL-196 is
   the sibling axis, untouched, not folded in.
3. **Defaults are authored per surface**, criterion = *answers its own question in one screenful at
   1280×720*; `lo` = the fixed rect's authored level, or `glance` where the container scrolls.
   Yields Read / Read / Read / **Glance** / Read / **Study**. **Rejected: Glance everywhere** — a
   fixed-rect container cannot shrink, so a Glance Selection band spends 340 px on emptiness.
4. **The level is remembered per surface, session-only, not serialised**; a subject change does not
   reset it, a new campaign does.
5. **The wizard participates**, with the sole named exception to the default criterion
   (`def = study`) and a reset-to-Study on entering the generation screen. **Rejected: exempting
   it** — exemption by omission is what created this item, and participation makes the wizard the
   idiom's teacher.
6. **Prose is a Study-only content class — withheld, never truncated.** Legend *values* stay at
   Read (a load-bearing figure); threshold *captions* move to Study (an annotation).
7. **Levels are strictly additive**, expressed as the single monotone `shows()` predicate with no
   `else` branch anywhere.
8. **Every guaranteed-fit container is Glance-only**, so drill-through adds no tenth container and
   can never create a new overflow site.
9. **The stepper is exempt from the toggle rule** as a cross-cutting selector (no null member in
   the set); re-click is a no-op, **not** revert-to-default. No `io-standing-rules.md` edit; the
   exemption is recorded in LAYOUT.md citing the rule's existing clause.
10. **No keyboard binding and no place on the Esc ladder** — `card_stack` already owns that unwind
    and depth must not double-book it.
11. **BL-214 lands before BL-215**, with the whether/how seam stated; the two run sequentially,
    not as concurrent worktree agents.

### Decisions taken on Ben's behalf (2026-07-30)

Ben delegated these calls for the ultracode session and was unavailable; each is recorded here so it can be reviewed or overturned.

**Q. 1. How many disclosure levels, what are they called, and must every surface place itself on the ladder?**

- **Decision:** THREE levels — GLANCE / READ / STUDY — declared as a closed set in `enum class detail_level` (src/ui/detail_level.hpp). Every *dense* surface declares itself on the ladder, but as an inclusive RANGE `[lo, hi]` plus a `def`, not as all three rungs. A surface whose `lo == hi` is single-level, draws no depth control, and is thereby explicitly on the ladder rather than silently outside it. Six surfaces are enumerated in the first landing: selection_band, selection_drill, history_story, history_chain, history_tiles, generation_wizard.
- **Why:** Two rungs is the collapse that produced the problem — 'compact vs full' is exactly what each of the four surfaces already invented separately; the useful middle rung ('the compact composed view') is where nearly every ledger actually sits today, so a two-value enum would force History's Chain and the Selection band to share a value they do not share. Four-plus is a spectrum, not a vocabulary, and LAYOUT.md's nine-container precedent is that the value comes from the set being closed and small. Three also maps 1:1 onto the three content classes the codebase already has: a figure, a chart, a paragraph. Declaring a RANGE rather than three rungs is what lets a Glance-only container (the header strip, the hover card) participate honestly instead of being an unstated exception — the same failure mode this item exists to kill.

**Q. 2. What is the uniform gesture — expand-in-place, child card (BL-196), or go-to? And must it mean the same thing everywhere?**

- **Decision:** The gesture is ONE shared control — `ui::detail_stepper`, a three-segment stepper — placed in a fixed position on every multi-level surface's title row (right-aligned, immediately LEFT of the `[>]` go-to / `[x]` close cluster), and EXPAND-IN-PLACE is the only permitted rendering response. Crucially, the answer also names what the other two gestures are, so they stop competing: they are not depth at all. Three orthogonal axes, three controls, never conflated — DEPTH (how much of this subject: the stepper, expand in place, BL-214); SUBJECT (what am I looking at: click the element, breadcrumb, child frame, BL-196's `ui.card_stack`); HOST (where does this live: `[>]`, `ui::focus_on_entity`, SELECTION.md's existing 'reference one hop away'). Yes, it means the same thing everywhere — that is the whole item.
- **Why:** The four idioms were never four answers to 'how do I show more'; they were three different QUESTIONS wearing one costume. The Corporation roll-up 'clicking through into a per-system ledger' is a host change. BL-196's child card is a subject change. Only the History explainer and the tile accordion's withheld derivation are depth. Once the axes are separated, BL-196 needs no folding-in and no competing — it is the sibling axis, and its breadcrumb (which is a SUBJECT-path indicator) is left exactly as built. A stepper rather than a cycling button because the level is state whose current value must be visible; a cycling button hides where you are, and an absolute selector never needs pressing twice. Expand-in-place is mandated because the 2026-07-23 UX note's finding was precisely that a mode-switch reads as 'the thing I was reading vanished', and because levels are strictly additive (Decision 6) the expansion is implementable top-down without moving anything already on screen.

**Q. 3. What is the default level per surface, and is it remembered?**

- **Decision:** The default is AUTHORED per surface in one table (`ui::detail_policy_of`), never computed at runtime. The authoring criterion: the default is the level at which the surface answers its own question in ONE SCREENFUL at 1280x720. That yields — selection_band READ, selection_drill READ, history_story READ, history_chain GLANCE, history_tiles READ, generation_wizard STUDY. A second derived rule fixes `lo`: a FIXED-RECT container's `lo` is the level its rect was authored for (so the 340px Selection band's `lo` is READ, not GLANCE); a stretch/scroll container's `lo` may be GLANCE. And YES, the player's chosen level IS remembered — per surface, for the session, in `ui_state::detail`, NOT serialised (same policy as `economy_view` / `history_view`). A subject change (selecting a different tile, switching body) does NOT reset it; a new campaign does, via `ui::reset_detail_levels`.
- **Why:** GLANCE-everywhere is the tempting answer and it is wrong for exactly one structural reason: a fixed-rect container cannot shrink. A GLANCE Selection band still occupies 340 fixed px (`selection_band_height`), so the level below the rect's authored level buys nothing and spends the band on dead space — density in a fixed rect beats emptiness. Where the container DOES stretch and scroll, GLANCE is honest and earns its keep: History's Chain at 324px column width fits four stage-verdict lines in one screenful and cannot fit four stages of charts, so its default drops to GLANCE and the item's instinct is vindicated by the rule rather than by assertion. Authored-not-computed because a default derived from the live region would twitch on resize, which is worse than any wrong constant. Remembered because a player who asks for depth is in a reading mood and will ask again in thirty seconds; making them re-ask each reopen is precisely the friction that makes depth feel expensive, which is the behaviour this item is trying to remove. Session-only because it is view state and the save format must not grow for it.

**Q. 4. Does the wizard participate?**

- **Decision:** YES — explicitly, and it is the one NAMED EXCEPTION to the default-authoring criterion. `generation_wizard` declares `lo = read, hi = study, def = study`. It does not fit STUDY in one screenful at 1280x720 and gets STUDY anyway, because for this surface the depth IS the feature. It is reset to STUDY on entering the generation screen from the main menu, so a fresh campaign always opens at full depth.
- **Why:** Exempting it by omission is what created this item, so it must participate or be named — and participating is strictly the stronger option for three concrete reasons. (a) It becomes the TEACHER of the idiom: the wizard is the first thing a player sees (BL-167), so meeting the stepper there means the gesture is already learned before the first ledger opens — the idiom's rollout is free. (b) A READ rung is a real want the exemption would have destroyed: a replaying player who has read ten stages of chemistry once wants the charts without the prose, and today has no way to ask. (c) 'First contact' is an argument about first contact specifically, which the reset-to-STUDY-on-entry rule honours exactly; it is not an argument for being outside the vocabulary. The exception is to the DEFAULT rule only, it is one row in the table, and it is written down rather than implied.

**Q. 5. Text density — how do the two-paragraph stage explainers behave, and how does this couple to BL-215?**

- **Decision:** Wrapped prose is a STUDY-ONLY content class. A paragraph is WITHHELD below STUDY — never truncated, never summarised, never demoted to a tooltip. Concretely: GLANCE renders figures, labels, verdict words and glyphs (no sentences); READ adds charts with their full legends (swatch, label AND value) and interactive sub-controls; STUDY adds wrapped prose, threshold captions, annotated axes, derivation breadcrumbs, and secondary/wide table columns. `stage_explainer()` renders at STUDY only. `charts::threshold_line`'s CAPTION is STUDY-only (the LINE itself is a chart element and stays at READ). The seam with BL-215 is stated flatly: **BL-214 decides WHETHER a string is drawn; BL-215 decides HOW a string that is drawn fits its container.** BL-214 lands FIRST, so BL-215's audit measures the reduced set and does not spend effort fitting strings this item withholds.
- **Why:** Truncating a paragraph is the LAYOUT.md ban being broken in a new place, and 'a shorter explainer' is content-cutting, which is the item's stated non-goal. Withholding is neither: the paragraph is intact and one click away. Legend VALUES are deliberately kept at READ rather than pushed to STUDY, because a legend value is a load-bearing figure and moving it up a rung would be truncation by another name — which is why the load-bearing invariant (Decision 6) exists. The BL-215 coupling is real and pays immediately: gating the threshold caption at STUDY removes, at the default level, the exact `"ay greenhouse"` clip that is committed in `scripts/verify/golden/history_chain_round0.png` today. Ordering BL-214 first avoids fixing that clip twice.

**Q. 6. What keeps this from being a content cut in disguise, and what is the invariant an implementer must not break?**

- **Decision:** LEVELS ARE STRICTLY ADDITIVE. A higher level never removes a load-bearing figure a lower level showed. Formally the whole model is one predicate: `shows(surface, ui, want) == (detail_level_of(surface, ui) >= want)`, and every content site is a single `if (shows(...))` branch — there is no `else`, no per-level layout variant, and no re-layout on level change. Second invariant, which is what makes the model safe against BL-215: EVERY GUARANTEED-FIT CONTAINER IS GLANCE-ONLY. LAYOUT.md containers 2 (lens legend), 4 (header strip), 5 (time panel), 7 (minimap lens bar) and 9-numeric (table cells) offer no depth control at all; levels only ever grow inside a WRAP container. Drill-through therefore adds NO tenth container — it is an orthogonal axis over the existing nine: the nine say how text fits, the three say how much text there is.
- **Why:** 'Expand, don't replace' (the 2026-07-23 UX note) is unenforceable as advice and trivial as an invariant — strict additivity makes it fall out of the implementation rather than out of discipline, since content drawn top-down and gated by a monotone predicate cannot move what is already on screen. The guaranteed-fit/Glance-only alignment is not a coincidence to be admired: it is the safety property. A container that measures text to size itself can never be handed a paragraph, so no level change can ever create a new overflow site — which is the one way this item could otherwise have made BL-215 worse instead of better.

**Q. 7. Does the depth stepper obey the universal toggle rule (re-clicking an active control undoes it)?**

- **Decision:** NO — it is EXEMPT, as a cross-cutting selector. Clicking the already-active segment is a no-op. This is recorded in LAYOUT.md citing the standing rule's existing exemption clause; `.claude/rules/io-standing-rules.md` is NOT edited. The stepper also takes no keyboard binding and does NOT join the Esc ladder in `app.cpp` (order today: confirm_exit -> system menu -> pop `card_stack` -> hide selection -> open system menu) — a level is not a dismissal and must not consume an unwind.
- **Why:** The standing rule exempts cross-cutting selectors 'which switch a target rather than express an active state', and the discriminating property is that a selector's set has NO NULL MEMBER — a resource combo has no null resource, and a surface always renders at SOME level. There is nothing for a toggle to undo TO. The clever reading ('re-click returns to the surface's default') is exactly the locally-clever/opaque solution the tone guidance rejects: it is invisible, unguessable, and it would make the one control in the app whose re-click means 'revert' sit next to nav_button strips whose re-click means 'close'. Staying off the Esc ladder matters because `card_stack` (SUBJECT) already owns an unwind there; giving DEPTH a second unwind would make Esc's meaning depend on invisible state, re-merging the two axes at the keyboard that Decision 2 just separated in the UI.
BL-214.resolution: Complete. Landed the BINARY fold model (Ben s 2026-07-31 supersession), not the three-level stepper: folded = a verdict line + a single chevron, expanded = a true full-screen overlay. State is one (surface, key) target rather than a per-surface remembered level - that falls out of expanded being an overlay, so only one thing can be expanded at a time. Six surfaces wired: the Selection band metric card, History Story/Chain/Tiles, the wizard s chain stages, and (via BL-248) the corp roll-ups. TWO CALLS TAKEN WITH BEN, asked with measurements: (a) the Selection band rests EXPANDED-IN-PLACE - its fixed 260px rect cannot shrink, so a folded one-liner would spend ~220px on emptiness, the objection the superseded design raised against Glance-everywhere and which the binary note never resolved; (b) the wizard folds PER CHAIN STAGE. ONE CALL TAKEN ALONE: the overlay JOINS the Esc ladder, one rung below the subject drills - Decision 10 kept depth off it, but reasoned about an in-place stepper, and a full-screen mode with no keyboard exit is a defect. The History Chain s per-stage CollapsingHeader was retired - it was this surface s own private idiom, the fourth one the item exists to kill. 10 goldens blessed and passing.

BL-217.design:
NOT YET SETTLED - this entry scopes the design pass, it does not close it. Read BL-210's full design field, PLANETOLOGY.md's preferences model (Round A/B/C, reject-and-reroll), and BL-208 (world-history-log, design-owed, v0.3.0) before designing.

## Open questions (carried and sharpened from BL-210)

1. **Where does branch state live?** Candidates: (a) extend `planetology_state` (today per-body, biosphere-scoped) to carry a generic checkpoint/branch list; (b) a new per-body structure parallel to it; (c) defer to BL-208's world-history-log once that lands, treating each checkpoint as a logged event with a branch tag rather than inventing separate storage. (c) is cheapest if BL-208's timeline allows it, but BL-208 is v0.3.0-scoped and this item is post-v0.1.0 - check whether checkpoint data can live provisionally in (a) and migrate to BL-208's log once it exists, rather than blocking on it.
2. **How does a lean bias a branch choice without becoming a probability slider?** BL-167's rule ('if you have preferences you can find them, but really you don't get full customization') must hold: reject-and-reroll stays the mechanism, a lean only narrows which branches are eligible to be proposed, never assigns them a visible weight.
3. **What counts as a checkpoint?** At minimum: the existing mass-extinction points (S5-S8) and the new historical-extinction point (settlement stage, BL-218). Confirm no additional checkpoints are needed before the two rewrites below start consuming this model - retrofitting a third checkpoint class after BL-218/BL-219 design lands is more expensive than settling the shape now.
4. **Viability floors.** Every branch must still fail against a homeworld-viability floor (BL-167's pattern) and reroll on failure - confirm this generalises cleanly or needs a per-checkpoint floor definition.

Does NOT need to settle: the specific historical-extinction branch outcomes themselves (that's BL-218's design), or the batch-sweep tool extension (an execution-depth follow-on once this model and BL-218/219 are settled, not a fourth design item).

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the four open questions

### 1. Branch state lives on the body's generation state, SHAPED so migration to BL-208 is a move

Option (c) — defer to BL-208's world-history-log — is the right destination and the wrong
dependency: BL-208 is v0.3.0-scoped, priority C, difficulty 5, and blocking a post-v0.1.0 item
behind it would park this chain indefinitely.

**Take (a), but make the provisional storage structurally identical to the log it will become.**
That is the whole design point, and it costs nothing to get right now:

    checkpoint_record { stage_id, branch_taken, seed_used, viability_result }

held as an **append-only, ordered, tagged** list on the body's generation state. Append-only and
ordered is exactly BL-208's log shape, so migration is a *move* — re-home the records, keep the
readers — rather than a rewrite. A random-access map keyed by stage, or a mutable
last-branch-wins field, would each be marginally more convenient now and would each make BL-208
a conversion project.

**Recording `seed_used` is not optional.** It is what makes a branch outcome reproducible in
isolation, which is what any future sweep tool and any bug report needs. A record that says
which branch fired but not from what seed cannot be replayed.

### 2. A lean is an ELIGIBILITY FILTER, never a weight

This is the question BL-167's rule most easily dies to, and the answer that preserves it is
structural rather than disciplinary.

**A lean removes branches from the proposal set. It never assigns a probability.** The choice
among the survivors stays the existing uniform reject-and-reroll. So a lean can make an outcome
*impossible*, and can never make one *more likely by a tunable amount* — which means there is no
slider to expose, no weight to tune, and no way for a preference to become a dial. "If you have
preferences you can find them, but you don't get full customization" falls out of the mechanism
instead of being enforced by taste.

**Corollary that must be built in, not discovered: if a lean filters every branch out, that is a
viability failure and the whole checkpoint rerolls.** It must not fall back to an ineligible
branch. Without this the lean silently stops mattering in exactly the cases where it was most
specific, which is the worst possible failure — the player's preference appears to be honoured
and is not.

### 3. Exactly TWO checkpoint classes, and a rule for admitting a third

- **Biological mass-extinction** — the existing S5-S8 points.
- **Historical rupture** — the settlement-stage point BL-218 introduces.

Confirmed: no third class is needed before BL-218/BL-219 start consuming this model.

**The rule for adding one, so this does not proliferate:** a checkpoint is a point where the
chain's *outcome distribution genuinely branches* — where two runs from the same prior state
can diverge into materially different worlds. It is **not** every point where something
interesting happens. An interesting event that does not change what the world can become is a
history-log entry (BL-208), not a checkpoint. Cheap to say now; expensive to relitigate once
three items consume the model.

### 4. Viability floors are PER-CHECKPOINT predicates over ONE mechanism

One global floor cannot work, because the two classes are not asking the same question. A
biological extinction's floor is *can this biosphere still reach sapience*; a historical
rupture's floor is *is there still a civilisation left to industrialise*. Forcing one predicate
over both makes it vacuous.

**So: one mechanism, per-checkpoint predicate.** Every floor has the same signature —
`(state) -> bool`, evaluated *after* the branch applies, reroll the checkpoint on false — and
each checkpoint class supplies its own. That generalises BL-167's pattern cleanly rather than
special-casing it, and the uniform signature is what lets the sweep tool treat all checkpoints
alike later.

**The homeworld rule still governs:** constrain the inputs, never clamp the outputs. A floor
rejects and rerolls; it never edits a result into viability.

S5-S8 biological die-off points retrofitted as checkpoints (5 recorded: Spark, Breath GOE + NOE, Green land-colonisation + fire-threshold) with zero change to the underlying biology/physics logic; S8/Legacy correctly excluded (no branch decision - logged as NR-027). ## What must survive the rewrite

- **The economic premise** (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md): a saturated, earth-like base the Nation AI owns as background, resource-carved markets (BL-096). The rewrite changes HOW a nation's territory/character/wealth are derived, not the shape of what the economy does with them afterward.

- **Determinism discipline**: per-stage hashed sub-streams, no bare transcendentals, the homeworld rule (constrain inputs, never clamp outputs) - same as every other stage in the chain.

## Open questions

1. **What replaces Pass 1-2 (seed placement + Voronoi BFS)?** A settlement-emergence model presumably seeds population centres on high-arable/high-river-connectivity tiles first (the continent/biosphere chain's own outputs), then grows territory as a consequence of historical competition rather than a pure geometric expansion. How much of the existing BFS/growth-weight machinery (Pass 1b/2, already tuned for size variance - BL-053) is reused vs replaced is a real cost question BL-210 asks to keep visible.
2. **What replaces Pass 4 (political character)?** Ideology/expansionism/economic_focus should emerge from the settlement/industrialisation history (a nation that industrialised early and had resource competition with a neighbour becomes 'expansionist', for instance) rather than an independent random draw. Needs a concrete derivation rule, not just a direction.
2a. **How does the historical-extinction checkpoint (BL-217) actually alter a nation's history?** - collapse, war, revolution as concrete effects on territory/character, not just a narrated line.
3. **Fragmentation.** NATION_GENERATION.md's open item on real historical fragmentation (exclaves, disputed zones - parked BL-054) may be substantially answered for free by a real settlement-history sim; confirm whether BL-054 folds into this item or stays separately parked.
4. **Cost comparison.** Per BL-210's own discipline, re-surface the cheaper alternative (keep Voronoi + richer narration only) as a comparison point even though Ben has already picked the deeper option three times running.

Does NOT need to settle: corporation industrial-focus derivation (BL-219, which consumes this item's output once settled).

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the four open questions

### 1. KEEP the growth machinery; replace what DRIVES it

The cost question the item asks to keep visible has a clean answer, and it is not "replace
Pass 1-2".

**Seeding changes. Expansion does not.** Population centres seed on tiles ranked by a score
already available from the continents/biosphere chain — arable capacity, river connectivity,
coastal access — rather than by the current placement. Territory then grows through the
**existing BFS/growth-weight machinery**, but with weights driven by *historical* pressure
(population growth, resource competition against an adjacent front) instead of a tuned
size-variance constant.

This matters because **BL-053 already tuned that machinery for size variance**, and that tuning
is real, hard-won value. Throwing it away to write a greenfield expansion model would cost the
most and regress a property that currently works. Reusing the mechanism and replacing its inputs
is both cheaper and keeps the tuned behaviour — the variance now *emerges* from differing
historical pressure rather than being dialled in, which is the actual goal.

### 2. Political character — a concrete derivation per axis

Each of the three axes derives from one specific quantity the settlement sim already produces.
Deterministic consequences of upstream scalars, not a fresh draw:

- **expansionism** <- **border-contest integral**: how often and how hard this nation's growth
  front met another's over the run. A nation that expanded into empty land is not expansionist;
  one that grew by pressing against neighbours is.
- **economic_focus** <- the **dominant resource class of the tiles it settled during
  industrialisation** — not of the tiles it merely holds. What a nation built on is what it
  becomes known for.
- **ideology** <- **industrialisation timing relative to neighbours**, plus first-mover versus
  catch-up. An early first-mover trends market/liberal; a late industrialiser catching up under
  competitive pressure trends statist/directed.

Each is computable from the run's own record and none needs a new roll. That is the standing
requirement — generation produces consequences, not dice.

### 2a. The historical-rupture checkpoint — three concrete transforms

The item demands effects on territory/character/wealth, "not just a narrated line". Each branch
is a transform on the nation's state:

- **Collapse** — territory contracts toward the surviving population centres; peripheral centres
  are lost; the industrialisation clock partially resets. Wealth falls; ideology unchanged.
- **War** — the border between the contesting pair redraws toward the stronger; both lose
  wealth; the loser's expansionism rises (grievance), the winner's confirmed.
- **Revolution** — territory unchanged; the **ideology axis flips**; wealth takes a one-off hit.
  The cheapest transform and the one that most changes how the nation later behaves.

Each also appends a biography line, but the line is a *record of* the transform, never a
substitute for it.

### 3. BL-054 SPLITS — it does not fold wholesale

The precise answer, because folding all of BL-054 in would quietly absorb a parked item that has
a second, unrelated half:

- **BL-054's territorial-fragmentation half** (exclaves, disputed zones) **folds into this
  item.** A real settlement sim produces them for free — a growth front that crosses a strait
  and stalls leaves an exclave without anyone authoring one. This is the single best argument
  for the deeper option, because the cheap alternative cannot produce it at all.
- **BL-054's nation-behaviour-passes half** (runtime nation AI) **stays parked and separate.**
  It is runtime behaviour, bounded by the standing rules, and has nothing to do with generation.

BL-054's own entry updated to record the split.

### 4. The cheaper alternative, surfaced honestly and rejected

Per BL-210's discipline: the cheap option is **keep Voronoi BFS and add richer narration** —
generate territory geometrically as today, then write history *describing* it.

**Rejected, and the reason is the one Ben has applied twice already elsewhere.** Narrating a
history over a geometric blob is the lying-figure objection (BL-256's globe caption, BL-263's
markets-with-no-cause): the prose would assert a settlement history the territory does not
reflect, and a player who reasons from the narration reasons wrongly. It also cannot produce
fragmentation (see 3), which is the concrete capability the deeper option buys.

Recorded rather than skipped because the item asks for it, and because Ben having chosen the
deeper option three times running is a reason to state the cheap one plainly, not to stop
offering it.

## What must survive the rewrite

- **Corporations stay specialists** (GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's economic premise) - lean, focus-coherent holdings, not a broad spread. This item changes WHY a corp has the focus it has, not the lean-holdings shape itself (that shape is separately load-bearing and already tuned).
- **Player corporation parity** - the player's corp is generated by the same pipeline as every rival, no special-cased generation rules (current invariant, stated in both NATION_GENERATION.md and CORPORATION_GENERATION.md).

## Open questions

1. **What in the nation's settlement history determines a corp's focus?** E.g. a nation whose settlement history shows early heavy industrialisation around ore provinces should tend to emit extraction/processing-focused corporations; a nation whose history reads as trade-hub/coastal should emit trade-focused ones. Needs a concrete derivation, not just plausibility.
2. **Does this retire the authored focus-weighting table entirely, or keep it as a fallback/tunable bias on top of the emergent signal?** A pure emergent derivation risks losing the 'diversity without enforcing a strict quota' property Pass 2 currently guarantees by construction.
3. **Post-WW2 industrial grounding** (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md's own open item) - this is the mechanism that item has been waiting for; the design pass should name which real-world industrial patterns (post-war extraction-to-manufacturing pipelines) the asset-mix derivation is modelled on, not treat it as automatically solved by 'derive from history'.
4. **Nation-seeded privatisation** (CORPORATION_GENERATION.md's own open item) - check whether this rewrite naturally produces a hook for nations seeding corporations into underserved industries, or whether that stays a separate follow-on.

Once this item and BL-218 are both settled and BUILT, BL-210's remaining scope (batch-sweep tool extension to lean x branch-combination space, and propagating the whole pivot into TILE_GENERATION.md/NATION_GENERATION.md/CORPORATION_GENERATION.md as settled authority) closes the umbrella.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the four open questions

### 1. Focus derives from the corp's HOME PROVINCE industrial history, not the nation average

A nation-level average would make every corporation in a nation look alike, which destroys the
specialist premise this item is required to preserve.

**A corporation's focus follows the industrialisation history of the province it is anchored
to.** The pipeline already places a corp's founding holdings somewhere; that somewhere has a
settlement/industrialisation record from BL-218. Read it: a province that industrialised around
ore emits extraction/processing corps; a coastal trade province emits trade-focused ones.

This gives within-nation variety for free — two corps in the same nation differ because their
provinces differ — while keeping each one coherent, which is exactly the "specialists, not
full-chain industrialists" shape.

### 2. The authored table is retired as a per-corp bias, and replaced by a world-level REROLL

The item is right that pure emergence risks losing Pass 2's "diversity without enforcing a
strict quota" property. But keeping the authored table as a per-corp fallback bias would mean
two mechanisms deciding the same field, which is how the field ends up unexplainable.

**Use the idiom the rest of the chain already uses: reject-and-reroll at the world level.**
Derive every corporation's focus emergently. Then, once, check world-level diversity against a
floor (no focus class wholly unrepresented). If it fails, **reroll the corporation set** — not
patch individual corps.

Why this is better than a per-corp fallback: a floor applied to the *set* is not a quota on any
*member*, so the diversity property survives without any corporation's focus becoming
inexplicable. It is also the same reject-and-reroll mechanism as BL-167's viability floors and
BL-217's checkpoints, so it adds no new concept. The authored focus-weighting table is retired.

### 3. Post-WW2 grounding — the named pattern is MOVEMENT UP THE CHAIN

The item is right to insist this is not automatically solved by "derive from history". The
specific real-world pattern being modelled:

**Early industrialisers moved up the value chain; late industrialisers stayed extraction-heavy.**
A nation that industrialised early had time to develop processing and manufacturing on top of
its extraction base, so its corporations skew toward refined and product tiers. A nation that
industrialised late — or under a first-mover's competitive pressure — remained an extraction and
raw-export economy, and its corporations skew raw.

This is directly derivable from the **industrialisation-timing scalar BL-218 already produces**
for the ideology axis, so it is one mapping rather than new machinery: timing feeds both *how a
nation thinks* and *what tier its corporations operate at*. That coupling is itself a good
outcome — a late statist industrialiser with raw-heavy corporations is a recognisable and
coherent thing.

### 4. Nation-seeded privatisation — the HOOK arrives, the mechanism stays deferred

The rewrite does produce the hook, and it is now precisely expressible: **a nation with an
industrialised province and no corporation operating in that province's resource class is
exactly the "underserved industry" condition** that item has been waiting for. Before this
rewrite there was no way to state it; there is now.

**Building it stays a follow-on.** Nations seeding corporations at runtime is nation behaviour,
which the standing rules bound (io-standing-rules § Determinism), and the generation-time
version is a different feature from the runtime one. This item records that the condition is
now computable and stops there.

### Player-corp parity, restated

The player's corporation goes through this same derivation with no special case — same province
read, same emergent focus, same world-level reroll. The invariant is unchanged and is worth
re-stating because "the player should start somewhere reasonable" is the exact pressure that
would break it.

BL-220.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (from the docs/lore/HISTORY.md review). Filed separately and first because four items (BL-209, BL-211, BL-238, and the three HISTORY.md ladder items) all append to the same `history_event` stream, and discovering the timestamp problem mid-item means reworking every one of them.

## The defect

`src/world/planetology.hpp:121`:

```
struct history_event {
    float       gya = 0.0f;   ///< Billions of years before present.
    chain_stage stage = chain_stage::system;
    std::string event;
    std::string consequence;
};
```

`gya` is correct and legible for the deep-time chain it was built for - S0 accretion at 4.5, the GOE at 2.4, land colonisation at 0.5. It cannot express a historical date at all:

- 1450 CE is 5.1e-7 Gya. At `float` precision the whole of recorded history collapses into the last few representable steps before zero, so two events centuries apart can compare equal.
- The ledger prints `4.5 Gya` / `now`. There is no format that reads sensibly for both 4.5 Gya and 1687 CE from one field.
- Sorting is the real hazard: the biography is a single ordered list, and the historical stages interleave into the same list as the deep-time ones.

## The shape

One timestamp field that spans both regimes, not two parallel fields the consumers must branch on. Recommended: a **signed integer year relative to the campaign epoch** (1 Jan 1960, ERAS.md), wide enough for 4.5 Gyr - `int64_t years_before_epoch`, or a fixed-point pair if the harness prefers it. Deep-time lines carry a round number of years; historical lines carry an exact one. `gya` becomes a derived accessor for display, not storage.

Why an integer and not a double: PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism & cost already bans implementation-defined float behaviour from gate paths, and a timestamp that participates in sorting is effectively a gate path. Integer years sort exactly, tie-break deterministically, and serialise without a format decision.

## Display, which is the actual user-visible half

The existing ledger (`tile_inspector.cpp`, the "Generation History" section shipped in b90ba10) formats a dated two-column line. It needs a formatter that picks the unit from the magnitude, on PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation's "do not linearise deep time" rule:

| Magnitude | Reads as |
|---|---|
| > 1 Myr | `4.5 Gya`, `252 Mya` |
| 1 kyr - 1 Myr | `11,650 years ago` |
| within recorded history | `1687`, `-3200` |
| 0 | `now` |

This is a presentation rule, not a data one - the same field drives all four.

## Migration

Every current emitter writes `gya` directly (`planetology.cpp`, `continents.cpp`). The change is mechanical and the harness pins it: `planetology_harness` R1 (determinism) and R2 (four bodies land in their archetypes) both compare history contents, so a botched conversion fails loudly.

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. `int64_t` years vs a fixed-point pair - decide against how the eventual serialiser wants it (no serialiser exists today; PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism & cost notes bodies are few and inline-on-body_component is right).
2. Whether `chain_stage` gains the historical stages (BL-221/222/223 add them) or the historical ladder carries its own parallel enum. Prefer one enum - a single ordered biography is the whole presentation model.

Read PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation and § Determinism & cost, and the "Generation History" section in src/ui/tile_inspector.cpp, before promoting.

Deep-time emitters still date in Gya - the `say` lambda in run_planetology narrows the conversion in ONE place, so all ~50 call sites were untouched. Also: continents.cpp's biography sort promoted std::sort -> std::stable_sort (tied integer timestamps are order-unspecified under std::sort - a determinism hazard the float key merely made unlikely); planetology_harness `same()` now compares timestamps exactly, so R1 catches a nondeterministic date; and a static_assert in tile_inspector.cpp pins ::campaign_epoch_year against ui::fmt::campaign_epoch_year (the world layer cannot include a UI header, so the constant is a deliberate duplicate). New harness group R14 (R12 reserved by BL-209, R13 by BL-238), 34 assertions, covers the conversions, every format band AND BOTH EDGES OF EVERY BAND, total oldest-first ordering, and that a historical line interleaves between deep time and the epoch - the property BL-221/BL-222 build on. CORRECTION TO THIS ITEM AS FILED: the design claimed float would make 'two events centuries apart compare EQUAL'. BL-221.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-30 (Ben, HISTORY.md review). The load-bearing call: **the ladder DRIVES, it does not narrate.**

> "100% driven. We are escaping the previous view where input -> output is exactly determined. For now, we want data on what kinds of worlds are interesting, so it would actually be valuable to see many failure cases, and find out what parameters should be tweaked for interesting gameplay." (Ben, 2026-07-30)

Read as: the knob-to-outcome map stops being closed-form, because outcomes now emerge from stages interacting. **Determinism is untouched** - the pass stays a pure function of (campaign_seed, ...), per the standing rule and PLANETOLOGY.md § Determinism & cost. *Flagged for confirmation at doc-pass time: if Ben meant something stronger than "not closed-form", that is a standing-rule change and must be raised explicitly, not assumed here.*

The second half of that quote is a scope instruction as much as a tuning one: **failure cases are wanted output, not defects.** The ladder is never rejected for producing a fragmented, poor, or late-industrialising world. That is BL-240's measurement surface, and the reason rarity is sweep-tuned rather than clamped.

## Where this sits

BL-210 sketched `Settlement -> Industrialisation -> 1900s` and explicitly deferred its design. `docs/lore/HISTORY.md` is that design, arriving as a causal ladder rather than a single pass. It splits three ways by what each half drives:

| Item | Stages | Drives |
|---|---|---|
| **BL-221 (this)** | 0 Surplus, 1 Charter, 2 Fragmentation | region count / nation count / fragmentation (feeds BL-239) |
| BL-222 | 3 Capital, 4 Energy | S9 drawdown, first-industrialiser, industrial character |
| BL-223 | 5 Rupture, 6 Saturation | the campaign premise itself |

Stages 0-2 must run **before** BL-239 forms nations, because BL-239 already states its region count is "a function of habitable land area and its fragmentation" - and this ladder is what generates fragmentation as a quantity rather than an adjective.

## The three stages

**Stage 0 - Agrarian surplus.** Surplus food -> dense settlements -> division of labour -> strangers who must trade rather than share. Reads arable share, ocean fraction and river connectivity (BL-170) off the tile map and BL-238's domesticable-clade output. Emits a **cradle count**: how many independent agricultural origins the land supports, and where. HISTORY.md: "More cradles -> deeper eventual fragmentation (feeds Stage 2)."

Line: `"-XXXX: First granary cities on the {region} floodplain."`

**Stage 1 - The enforceable promise / the Charter Age.** Contract law extends past kinship: partnership, credit, then the charter - an entity that outlives its members and can own, sue, and be sued. HISTORY.md is correct that the game's own rule already IS this doctrine made mechanical: *"A corporation persists as long as it holds at least one asset"* (GLOSSARY.md, CONCEPT.md:7). No new mechanic is needed; the stage generates its **origin**.

The Kepler divergence HISTORY.md asks for is that the charter arrives EARLY relative to Earth, and that it is registered-in-a-home-nation-but-operationally-free - which is exactly the bargain CORPORATION_GENERATION.md already describes (taxable and seizable in exchange for freedom of operation). What this stage drives: which nation's legal tradition the charter came from, and how early - feeding corporate focus derivation in BL-239 step 4.

Line: `"YYYY: The {nation} Charter Act - first perpetual company registered."`

**Stage 2 - Fragmentation with connectivity.** Many competing states, close enough to trade, copy and poach; none able to conquer the rest. HISTORY.md's causal claim is the one worth keeping verbatim: *"A hegemon can CHOOSE stagnation - suppress a technology by decree and it stays suppressed. Forty-five rivals cannot: a capability banned in one polity re-emerges next door. Competition among states is the market mechanism applied to governance itself."*

The generator hook is the terrain barriers BL-239 already clusters on - mountain ranges, deserts, open water, absent arable land - now consumed a second time to decide how EXPENSIVE conquest is and how CHEAP exit is. Output: a fragmentation scalar plus the polity-seed count BL-239 grows nations from.

Line: `"YYYY: The {range} Peace - {n} realms confirm mutual borders."`

## What it drives (the whole point of "100% driven")

1. **Cradle count -> fragmentation -> region and nation count.** Today `nation_generation.cpp` seeds Voronoi arbitrarily and merges anything under `min_nation_tiles` (80). Under BL-239 the seeds come from culture regions; under this item the NUMBER of them is a historical outcome.
2. **Conquest cost / exit cost.** A single scalar pair from Stage 2's barrier read, consumed by BL-239's settlement-and-conflict growth and by BL-224's non-hegemony assertion.
3. **The charter's home tradition and date**, feeding corporate focus derivation.

## Presentation

Three lines into the existing biography, in the ledger shipped by b90ba10 (nav slot 9, "Generation History"). Every line carries its consequence in the right column - PLANETOLOGY.md § Presentation, non-negotiable. No codex, no separate surface: HISTORY.md's own open question 3 ("codex, generated lines, or ambient flavour?") is answered by the surface already existing.

Entries are authored into BL-208's append-only world log, not a parallel structure - same call BL-238 made, same reason.

## Determinism

Fresh stage tags per stage; per-stage hashed sub-streams (PLANETOLOGY.md warns 0x4A71012u is already folded twice in hard_coded_world.cpp). Cradle scoring and barrier costs are integer or fixed-point with an explicit tie-break by tile index - a float argmax over regions is a portability hazard and a tie-break nightmare, the same objection BL-239 raises for its trait vectors. No bare transcendentals in any gate path.

## Cut, by the diagnostic test

PLANETOLOGY.md: "for every generated value, name the decision it changes. Anything that fails is deleted, not tuned." Provisionally cut: **named historical polities and rulers** (worldbuilding, changes nothing); **a coinage/currency stage** (HISTORY.md itself argues the deep enabler is the enforceable promise, not coinage - so coinage is a line at most, never a gate); **writing/literacy as its own gate** (real, invisible downstream).

## Residual calls (doc-pass time)

1. Whether Stage 0-2 are three gates with failure states (a world with too few cradles never fragments, and gets a hegemon - which BL-224 then has to assert against) or three scored passes with no failure. Ben wants failure cases visible, which argues for gates.
2. Whether the fragmentation scalar is one number or a per-region field. Per-region is truer and is what BL-239's clustering would rather consume.
3. Ordering against BL-239 in detail: this item produces seeds, BL-239 grows polities, and Stage 2's "n realms confirm mutual borders" line can only be written AFTER growth. So the ladder interleaves with BL-239 rather than strictly preceding it - specify the interleave.
4. Whether the ~45 nations HISTORY.md asserts is a target for this stage or an emergent number. Today's build generates 14 (BL-094 references "the 14 generated Voronoi nations"), so the gap is 3x and someone must own it.

Read docs/lore/HISTORY.md in full, BL-239's mechanism section, BL-210's settlement-stage sketch, and NATION_GENERATION.md before promoting.

BL-226.design:
SETTLED 2026-07-30 (Ben session). Ben chose option B (return + retain the plate field) over A (flood-fill contiguous landmasses at render time) and C (persist continent_state to the save).

WHY B. A shows LANDMASSES, not plates — it can colour the continents but cannot explain them, because the thing worth showing is the BOUNDARY (where the mountain range, the rift and the porphyry copper came from), and a boundary is invisible once the height bias has been folded into the heightmap. C buys nothing over B and touches the save format for presentation data.

THE DATA PATH.
1. continent_state gains `std::vector<int> plate_id` (row*gw+col). The Voronoi loop already computed this in a local; it is now written to the out-param. Sized before the stagnant-lid early return so every consumer sees a full-length field (all-zero = one immobile plate).
2. generation_report::body_entry gains `continent_state continents`. Its `history` is MOVED into state.history at generation as before and then cleared, so the biography stays the single owner of those lines and nothing is stored twice. The report is presentation data the app holds for the session — it never enters `world`, so this stays off the serialisation seam (same reasoning as world_params, BL-114).
3. draw_body_surface_canvas takes `const generation_report&` and matches the active body by NAME — the same stable key the Tile Ledger's biography already uses (body_entry carries no entity_id).
A missing entry or a size mismatch leaves the pointer null: the lens then draws plain terrain and its key says 'No plate record' rather than inventing plates.

THE RENDER. Plate tint at 0.80 (this lens is about the plate field, not the terrain under it) with a separate white lift at 0.45 on any tile whose 4-neighbourhood crosses a plate — columns wrap, rows do not. The boundary MUST read on a different channel from the plate colour: the first draft used 'the same colour, blended harder' and the boundaries were invisible on capture.

THE PALETTE. A dedicated table, not palette::nation_colour — plates are substrate, not identity, and borrowing the vivid nation wheel would make this read as a second Country lens. But it must still be CATEGORICAL: the first draft's muted mineral tones (all luminance ~100-130, tiny hue spread) collapsed into one grey wash on capture and the lens could not tell one plate from the next. Final table keeps the earthy cast but alternates light/dark so adjacent slots differ even in greyscale. Ten slots covers run_continents' 4..10 clamp.

STRIP SLOT. Added as the EIGHTH on-strip lens rather than the keyboard-only shelf: it answers a question the player asks at first sight of a body ('why is the land shaped like that?'), which is the moment they are looking at the strip. Confirmed to fit the 240px minimap bar on capture.

VERIFICATION. scripts/verify/continents_terrain.lua gains continent-lens captures on Kepler and Selene (the small-grid body, which also exercises a differing plate count and the key's layout). The plate boundaries in the lens capture should line up with the ridges and coastlines in the plain-terrain capture from the same script — that correspondence IS the check that the lens is showing the field the terrain was derived from.

OPEN. The lens key is occluded by the Tile Ledger when that panel is open, since the key hangs off the minimap's left edge — this is pre-existing behaviour shared by every lens key, not specific to this item, but it was noticed here and is worth its own item.

BL-231.design:
DESIGNED 2026-07-31 (Ben session — arose from the question "do we need a more diverse set of tiles?", and the observation that mountains and hills have no visual render).

## The finding: this is a RENDER gap, not a content gap

The two-axis model already carries 11 compositions x 7 landforms (TILES.md), and generation
genuinely produces all of them — tile_generation.cpp Pass 5 grows mountain, rift and crater
clusters from seeds, then fills remaining low ground as valley.

But `terrain_colour` (src/ui/hex_render.cpp:17) switches on COMPOSITION ONLY — eleven flat
colours. Landform never reaches the screen. Mountain, highland, canyon, valley, crater and rift
all render as the flat hex of whatever they are made of. Six of the seven landforms are invisible.

So the answer to "should we add more tile types" is NO. The set is not thin; the renderer is
discarding half of it. Widening the model before drawing what it already has would make the gap
bigger, not smaller.

hex_render.hpp:23 already asserts that "landform is conveyed by glyphs, not hue". No landform
glyph exists anywhere in icons.hpp — the comment documents an intention nobody built. It becomes
true (or gets deleted) as part of this item.

## Why it is worth fixing

The invisible axis is mechanically load-bearing, not decorative:

- build cost x1.0 -> x2.0 (TILES.md § Terrain landform)
- hazard +0.05 -> +0.30 and habitability x0.60 -> x1.15 (tile_generation.cpp:752-758)
- deposit richness — mountain and rift boost minerals (TILES.md § deposit tables)

The player pays a doubled build cost for terrain the map never showed them. That is the same class
of legibility hole BL-071 (build legibility) and BL-179 (workforce reason on select) closed
elsewhere: the sim consumes a quantity the surface never states.

## SETTLED — always-on chrome, NOT a lens

Landform is terrain IDENTITY, the same kind of thing as composition hue — not a data overlay the
player opts into. The build-cost multiplier applies whether or not a lens is active, so the read
must be always-on and must survive under every lens, alongside the settlement markers and the
BL-085 player identity chrome. No new `overlay_mode`. Authority is CANVASES.md, not LENSES.md.

## SETTLED — the channel constraint

BL-226's hard-won lesson stands: a second signal must read on a DIFFERENT CHANNEL from the first,
or it vanishes. Composition owns HUE (TILES.md: composition determines visual identity), and lens
tints composite over that hue at 0.6-0.80 alpha. So landform cannot be hue, and cannot be a flat
fill modulation — either would be obliterated exactly when a lens is on.

Three channels exist. GLYPH (the hex centre) is crowded: the building marker, corp emblem tag,
value mark, convoy, market centre and settlement all draw at or near {cx, cy}. EDGE is precedented
and mostly free (the Country lens strokes differing-owner edges; the Continent lens lifts boundary
tiles). INTERIOR TEXTURE is entirely unused today.

## SETTLED — mirror Pass 5's own three tiers

Generation already sorts landforms into three structural roles. The render should mirror that
rather than invent its own grouping:

- FEATURE CORES — mountain, rift, crater. Grown as clusters from seeds (`grow_cluster`, ring 0).
  Categorical KINDS, not degrees; sparse by construction.
- APRONS — highland, canyon. What rings 1-2 decay into around a core (`landform_for_ring`).
- FILL — plains (the baseline) and valley (unclaimed low ground, height < 0.35).

That split maps cleanly onto two channels:

- Feature kind is CATEGORICAL -> GLYPH. Three glyphs, drawn only on cluster cores, so glyph density
  stays near the existing marker families rather than pebbling every land tile.
- Elevation is ORDINAL (mountain > highland > plains > valley) -> an EDGE/RELIEF channel, which
  shows the SHAPE of a range instead of repeating an identical icon per tile.

Neither channel alone is sufficient, and this is the reason the item is not a one-liner. Contours
alone cannot tell a crater from a rift (those are kinds, not elevations). Glyphs alone put an icon
on every land tile — denser than any existing glyph use — and fight the building marker for the
centre. Two channels, matching the generation's own structure, is the composable answer.

## STEP 1 IS MEASUREMENT — do not skip

The glyph/relief proportion depends on how many tiles are actually feature cores, and NOBODY KNOWS.
world_audit has a COMPOSITION histogram (tools/verify/world_audit.cpp:27) and no landform histogram
at all. If mountain cores are 30% of a body, a per-tile glyph is noise and the relief channel must
carry the read; if they are 3%, the glyph is right and relief is a whisper.

So the first task is to extend world_audit with a per-body composition x landform histogram, run it,
and RECORD THE NUMBERS IN THIS ITEM before the proportions are fixed. This pays back beyond the
item: the same histogram is what BL-240 (generation sweep) will want, and it is the standing check
that a future tuning change has not quietly flattened the landform mix. Per CLAUDE.md § Tool
creation is skill creation, it lands in the committed harness, not as a one-off.

## OPEN — resolved during the build, against a live capture

These are look judgements, not structural gaps. Each is settled by putting the app in front of Ben
(standing rule: open the live app when asking him to weigh in on visuals), not by more prose.

1. GLYPH VS RELIEF WEIGHT. With the histogram in hand: does relief carry most of the read (subtle,
   map-like) with glyphs reserved for the three feature cores — or do glyphs carry it and relief
   stay a whisper? Recommendation is the former; it needs the numbers and an eyeball.
2. GLYPH ON A BUILT TILE. A built tile is swapped wholesale for its owner plate
   (body_surface_canvas.cpp:1473) and already carries a building silhouette plus a corp emblem tag.
   Suppressing the landform glyph there loses the build-cost read at exactly the tile where the
   cost was paid; keeping it risks a three-glyph hex.
3. HEIGHTMAP OR LANDFORM CLASS for the relief channel. Pass 1's heightmap is finer but is not
   retained — the same retention problem BL-226 solved for `plate_id`, and solvable the same way.
   Landform class is already on the tile and needs no plumbing. START WITH LANDFORM CLASS; only
   reach for the heightmap if the ordinal read proves too coarse.

## Terminology

The canonical word for hills is HIGHLAND (TILES.md § Terrain landform). Keep it — GLOSSARY
discipline; do not introduce "hills" as a second name for the same thing.

## Related, deliberately not folded in

BL-051 (tile generation refinements) parks TECTONIC landforms as speculative GENERATION work; this
item is render-only and needs no generation change. GENERATION_LEDGER.md designs a heightmap field
overlay for TUNING — a different surface for a different audience (that one is a lens for the
developer; this is always-on chrome for the player). BL-226 (continent lens) is the adjacent
precedent for both the channel rule and, if open question 3 goes that way, the data-retention
pattern.
